enonce_markdown: A hand specimen is made of well-rounded pebbles 5 to 30 mm across set in a sandy matrix and cemented together. What is the rock?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Name a clastic rock from the size of its clasts first, then from their shape: rounded gravel gives a conglomerate and angular gravel a breccia.

### Solution

Pebbles (grain size above 2 mm) make the rock a rudaceous rock. Because they are **rounded**, it is a **conglomerate**. A breccia has angular clasts, siltstone has grains below 0.0625 mm, and a quartz arenite is a sandstone with grains of 0.0625 to 2 mm.

**Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown: A sandstone is described as well sorted. What does this tell you about the rock?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Sorting describes the spread of grain sizes; roundness describes corners; sphericity describes overall form; cement describes how grains are held together.

### Solution

Sorting is the uniformity of grain size. A well-sorted rock has grains of similar size (as in a dune or beach sand). Angularity is a matter of roundness, near-spherical form is sphericity, and the cement is a separate feature of the rock.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The grains are bound by a strong cement
The grains have sharp, angular corners
Most of the grains are of about the same size
The grains are nearly spherical in overall shape

enonce_markdown: A fine-grained white rock gives no reaction with cold dilute hydrochloric acid on a lump, but fizzes steadily when scratched to a powder. It is made of a single carbonate mineral. Which rock is it most likely to be?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Calcite effervesces strongly with cold dilute acid even as a lump, dolomite only when powdered, and silica minerals do not react at all.

### Solution

A carbonate that reacts only when powdered is **dolomite**, so the rock is a dolostone. A calcite limestone would fizz vigorously on the lump, and both chert and quartz arenite are made of silica, which does not react with dilute HCl even as a powder.

**Answer: A.**

enonce_markdown: Which description fits an immature sandstone?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Maturity increases with the removal of clay, better sorting, more rounding and the loss of unstable minerals such as feldspar and rock fragments.

### Solution

Immature means little changed by weathering and transport: angular, poorly sorted grains, unstable minerals (feldspar) and plenty of clay matrix, usually deposited close to the source. The sandstones with 98 % quartz and with well-rounded, well-sorted grains are mature to supermature, and the one with little feldspar and no clay is more mature than immature. The nature of the cement (calcite) has no bearing on maturity.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Well-rounded, well-sorted quartz grains held by calcite cement
Well-sorted, sub-rounded grains with 10 % feldspar and no clay matrix
Angular grains of quartz and feldspar, poorly sorted, in an abundant clay matrix
Well-rounded, well-sorted grains that are 98 % quartz with no clay

enonce_markdown:
A 200 g sample of a lithified sediment is disaggregated and sieved. The mass retained is 14 g above 2 mm, 130 g between 2 mm and 0.0625 mm, and 56 g passing 0.0625 mm (silt and clay).

(a) Calculate the percentage of gravel, sand and mud in the sample.

(b) A sandstone that contains more than 15 % fine matrix is called a wacke. Is this rock a wacke? Give your reasoning.

(c) What does the high matrix content suggest about the sorting and the textural maturity?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Percentage of a fraction = mass of the fraction / total mass x 100. Fine matrix content is a measure of textural maturity: the more clay and silt remain, the less mature the sediment.

### Solution

(a) Gravel: $14/200 \times 100 = 7\ \%$. Sand: $130/200 \times 100 = 65\ \%$. Mud: $56/200 \times 100 = 28\ \%$. The three add up to 100 %.

(b) Sand is the main fraction (65 %), so the rock is a sandstone, and the matrix (28 %) is above 15 %, so it is a **wacke** (a muddy sandstone).

(c) A mixture of gravel, sand and mud means the grain sizes are very mixed, so the rock is **poorly sorted**. A large amount of clay matrix that has not been winnowed out means the rock is **texturally immature**, typical of rapid deposition with little reworking, for example from a turbidity current.

enonce_markdown:
Two sandstones were described in the field.

Sandstone P: 97 % quartz grains, all about 0.3 mm in diameter, well rounded with a frosted (pitted) surface, no clay, thick sets of large cross-beds with steeply inclined laminae.

Sandstone Q: grey-green, grains of angular quartz, feldspar and dark rock fragments from 0.05 to 2 mm, about 25 % clay matrix, in beds 20 to 50 cm thick that each become finer upwards from a sharp base.

(a) Name the type of each sandstone and state which is more mature, with two reasons.

(b) Suggest the most likely depositional environment of each.

(c) Explain how the beds of Q record the way the sediment was deposited.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Combine composition, texture and structures: composition and rounding give the maturity, sorting and bedding give the energy and the mode of deposition.

### Solution

(a) P is a **quartz arenite** (a supermature sandstone): the grains are almost pure quartz (97 %), well sorted, well rounded and free of clay. Q is a **greywacke** (lithic wacke): angular, poorly sorted grains of several minerals and rock fragments set in abundant clay matrix, so it is **immature**. P is clearly the more mature of the two.

(b) P: a **desert dune** (aeolian) setting, shown by the frosted, well-rounded grains and large cross-beds from migrating dunes (a beach is also acceptable). Q: **deep-water marine turbidite** deposition on a slope or basin floor, beyond the reach of waves, close to a rapidly uplifted source.

(c) Each bed of Q is **graded**: the sharp base shows a sudden strong current that eroded the sea floor, and the upward fining shows the sediment settling out as the current lost energy, coarse grains first and the fine ones last, all in a single event. The clay matrix remains because there was no time for winnowing.
